io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publish.long_description: AI agent for SAP analytics and AI consultants. Curated, source-backed intelligence on the SAP analytics services market (Datasphere, Business Data Cloud, SAP Analytics Cloud, BW/4HANA, Databricks), exposed read-only so an assistant can answer precisely and cite the exact record. SIXTEEN tools: ELEVEN public and unauthenticated, plus FIVE a subscriber key opens (listed and refusing by name, never hidden): a directory of SAP consulting, recruitment and vendor organisations searchable by country and kind, with a profile per firm, plus an aggregate count over it for an agent that needs a number rather than a page of rows; a published day-rate aggregate by geography, stack and seniority — small, all secondary sources, sample_size null where no observation matches the cell, and GBP/CHF never folded into the euro rows; a live contract radar of publicly published SAP analytics openings, the same 2,490 rows an anonymous visitor browses, each with its own page — filter it by employment_type, because it is mostly PERMANENT roles (2,172 of 2,381 on 2026-08-11) and an unfiltered page answers a contracting question with salaried jobs; 1,421 rows carry a panel-inferred P25-P75 day-rate band for their seniority x product x region cell, served with its basis, kind, sample and source so it is never quotable as the employer's own offer; what is gated there is a FIELD, not a row — the verified link to the original listing is the Consultant deliverable and reads members_only on 2,375, while every other fact, and the page, stay public; a curated market-news corpus de-duplicated by upstream URL, its size read at query time and returned as _meta.match_count rather than quoted from here, each item carrying the upstream publisher's URL alongside ours; a concept encyclopaedia of the stack's vocabulary; the SAP module lookup; and the metadata of 38 study editions on market structure, day rates and recruiter economics — 19 deep-research studies, each in EN and FR, so the tool returns editions and counting rows gives 38 where counting studies gives 19. Read-only: every tool is annotated readOnlyHint. The eleven public tools need no credential; the five paid ones come with an analyticslegends.ai subscription (Consultant or above) or the MCP Pass (€39/month, analyticslegends.ai/pricing/). Retrieval with attribution is permitted, training is not; every response carries a citation_url for the record served. DELIBERATELY NOT SERVED at any tier: the opportunity-to-consultant matchers, and people — consultants are held as initials only and no tool returns anyone's identity or contact details. SAP's own documentation is not ours to restate: cite SAP.
